findings.claim: The fr4 fix broadened the except clause correctly but did not deliver the two regression tests that were the second half of the R4 MAJ mitigation: a test monkey-patching subprocess.run to raise subprocess.TimeoutExpired and a test raising OSError (e.g. FileNotFoundError when git is absent), each asserting key_id is None, error field populated, and all static resources still served.
findings.evidence: test_signing_keys_outage.py contains exactly two test functions: test_snapshot_degrades_when_committed_signing_keys_are_malformed (multiple-current-key → RuntimeError path) and test_snapshot_logs_and_degrades_for_empty_committed_signing_keyring (empty keyring → RuntimeError path). Grep across tests/scp_mcp/ for TimeoutExpired or OSError matches only test_tools/test_audit_changed.py, which is unrelated to signing-key degradation. R4 mitigation text (review-safety.json structured_review.findings[0].mitigation) explicitly required: 'Add a test in test_signing_keys_outage.py that monkey-patches subprocess.run to raise subprocess.TimeoutExpired and asserts the snapshot degrades (key_id is None, error field is populated, remaining static resources are still served).' No such test exists.
findings.impact: The except clause is correct in production today. The risk is forward-looking: a future refactor that narrows the except clause back to RuntimeError-only would pass the existing test suite undetected, silently re-opening the SB-R4-MAJ-001 attack surface. Given that the 021H HTTP transport (which makes the subprocess.TimeoutExpired vector more reachable) is on the slice roadmap, this gap will grow more consequential once HTTP ships.
findings.mitigation: Add two tests to tests/scp_mcp/test_resources/test_signing_keys_outage.py. (1) Patch subprocess.run in the git-show call path to raise subprocess.TimeoutExpired(cmd=['git','show'], timeout=30) and assert snapshot.key_id is None, signing_keys['error'] contains 'TimeoutExpired' or similar, all STATIC_RESOURCE_URIS still return a payload. (2) Patch subprocess.run to raise FileNotFoundError('git not found') and assert the same degradation invariants. No production code changes required — the _degraded_signing_keys_payload path is already correct.

self_reported_concerns: SB-R5-MIN-001 severity: rated MIN rather than MAJ because the production code fix (except clause) is present and correct; the gap is purely in regression-detection, not in active bypassability. If 021H HTTP transport ships before this test is added, reassess as MAJ because the TimeoutExpired vector becomes trivially reachable via a 30-second network partition.

The TOCTOU race in snapshot() (HEAD read before lock acquisition at resources.py:463) is a pre-existing bounded staleness window acknowledged across all prior rounds. Under the SAFETY_BYPASS lens it does not constitute a new finding: the worst case is serving a snapshot that is one commit stale, which does not expose an adversarially-controlled signing key or bypass any access check. Not re-opened.

_subscribers dict access (subscribe/unsubscribe at resources.py:481–489) is not protected by _snapshot_lock. Under CPython with GIL, individual dict and set operations are atomic, so the practical risk is limited to missed notifications rather than a security bypass. Noted but not filed as a finding under the safety-bypass lens.
All findings are based on static code analysis and inspection of test file contents. The test suite was not executed.
structured_review.summary: R5 safety-bypass review of slice 021D after fr4. One R4 MAJ carry-forward (SB-R4-MAJ-001 — too-narrow except clause in _build_snapshot) is confirmed CLOSED: resources.py:581 now reads `except (RuntimeError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired, OSError) as error:` with explanatory comments at lines 582–587 covering all three exception classes. No regression on any previously-closed R1/R2/R3 finding: path-traversal is blocked by _resolve_repo_relative_path/_normalise_repo_relative_path with container-escape rejection; threading.Lock at resources.py:452 guards the snapshot build with correct double-checked locking; raw public-key bytes are absent from the signing-keys response; prior_keys list is built from current_key_id so the dead-branch None leak is closed; waivers.json is read once per snapshot cycle. No new CRIT or MAJ findings under the safety-bypass lens. One MIN finding: the R4 MAJ mitigation specified adding tests that monkey-patch subprocess.run to raise TimeoutExpired and OSError and assert degraded-snapshot behaviour; those tests were not delivered. test_signing_keys_outage.py still carries only the two RuntimeError degradation tests (malformed keyring, empty keyring). The production safety invariant holds today because the except clause is correct, but the regression-detection surface is incomplete. §4.3 fixpoint is reached: no CRIT or MAJ findings remain.
